pr_body:
This is a reboot of sorts on the macos_userdefaults resource to fix some fundamental flaws in the UX of the resource and how it gets state / sets the values.

Fixes https://github.com/chef/chef/issues/7622
Fixes https://github.com/chef/chef/issues/10095
Fixes https://github.com/chef/chef/issues/10084

**The good:**

- Uses the array format of values for `shell_out`, which avoids the previous issues with spaces in keys/values
- Rewrites how we load state to use `defaults export`, which allows us to parse complex data values accurately. The previous method of determining the current value just used grep for a string, which would fail on anything but the most basic value
- Overall this fixes a bunch of small failures to set values correctly. Things just didn't work throughout and unit testing exposed much of that.
- By properly loading state we now get much better convergence logging that shows before and after state. 
- Add a new `:remove` action for removing keys entirely. This seemed like a useful thing that was missing
- Replaced the 'global' property with a default value in the `domain` property instead. Previously it was meant that you could set the global property and skip domain to get `NSGlobalDomain` as your domain. Seems a bit overly complex to have two properties that control the domain, but you know whatever. Unfortunately, this didn't work because in `load_current_value` we still tried to load from the domain property and this would result in a domain of '' which would blow up the defaults command. So it's really questionable if this is a breaking change since it didn't work before. Now if you skip the domain property you just get the default of `NSGlobalDomain`. I'm fairly confident that no one ever used this, but I can create a Cookstyle rule if we want to be extra sure.
- Added specs for the `defaults export` and `defaults write` commands to validate how we build the commands for getting and setting state
- Added a better description to sudo to explain the requirements of setting this. 
- Added equal_to to the type property since it was entirely undocumented what values were allowed here. Since we don't support every defaults type you had to just read to code to know how to use it. 
- Added a new `host` property that lets you set per-host values. If you set this to :current it sets the `-currentHost` flag.
- Set desired_state to false on everything that isn't a state property
- Removes the `is_set` property which was being used to store the state

**The bad:**

This updated resource does a much better job of handling complex data types, but it's still deeply flawed since it relies on the `defaults` command, which can't set complex nested values. We could push it further, but we're close to the limits.


**Things I'm going to tackle in subsequent PRs:**

- booleans that are specified as strings with the type set to bool are not idempotent
- we need more examples

Signed-off-by: Tim Smith <tsmith@chef.io>
pr_comments:
I think continuing to coerce the values is not ideal, because it's not truly desired state if you can cheat the system.

Doing something like https://github.com/chef/chef/issues/10086 seems more appropriate here so you can truly compare the real values.

@erikng Can you elaborate on "cheat the system". I'll freely admit that this is less than ideal, but I think it potentially gives us the performance we need while determining state (if done right). I'm not super opposed to exporting the data to get the current state, but I'd need to see various perf benchmarks there to show that we're not going to take a significant hit by adding that file io. Even if this method gets tossed in a few months I think the other bits of refactoring here are valuable to continue and certainly worth shipping as soon as possible.

@erikng I ran into the truthy issues today which led me to look at the perf of the export. It's actually not bad so I'm going to see what it takes to at least load current value with that. More changes incoming here.

## Chef Version

## Platform Version
